fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled glyph-data offsets from the input font's sbix table. imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] can be 0 (null) and is compared, but is never checked with is_null() before being dereferenced later.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned int delta = imageOffsetsZ[old_gid + 1] - imageOffsetsZ[old_gid];
      unsigned int glyph_data_length = delta - SBIXGlyph::min_size;
fine_trace.note: Copy length is derived from attacker-controlled offsets: with imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]=0 (null) and imageOffsetsZ[old_gid+1]=488, delta=488 and glyph_data_length becomes 480 bytes.

Root cause: the missed is_null() check on imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]. For offset value 0 the expression 'this + imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]' evaluates to Null(SBIXGlyph), i.e. a pointer into the 384-byte static _hb_NullPool, and copy() is asked to read glyph_data_length bytes from it.
SBIXGlyph::copy forwards the oversized length (glyph_data_length) to the raw byte-array copy; data sits at offset 8 of the Null(SBIXGlyph) object, i.e. _hb_NullPool+8.

Sink: element-by-element copy reads count=480 bytes starting at _hb_NullPool+8. The global _hb_NullPool is only 384 bytes (HB_NULL_POOL_SIZE), so the reads for bytes 384..487 go out of bounds (ASAN global-buffer-overflow).

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The public issue states the sbix subset implementation misses an is_null() check on an offset, leading to unsafe memory access. In SBIXStrike::subset a glyph-data offset imageOffsetsZ[old_gid] equal to 0 is not rejected: 'this + imageOffsetsZ[old_gid]' then resolves to the static Null(SBIXGlyph) object backed by the 384-byte _hb_NullPool, and SBIXGlyph::copy/UnsizedArrayOf::copy reads glyph_data_length bytes from _hb_NullPool+8, exceeding the pool (global-buffer-overflow) whenever imageOffsetsZ[old_gid+1] > 384.
